title: a kill in the window between ingest() returning and the .committed marker being written makes startup recovery restore the OLD rows over a complete new session (consistent, but the finished re-transcription/embedding work is discarded and must be paid for again)
evidence: reingest-crash.test.mjs 'kill after ingest returned but BEFORE the commit marker was written': recovery output is byte-identical to the pre-reingest state, new session removed. The window is one small atomic file write.
fix_direction: none needed for safety; to save the work, write the marker from inside ingest() before its last step, or have recovery compare the new session's turns/chunks to the Drive file and keep it when complete.

title: type exactness is proven only against the in-memory BSON-bytes fake: rows read through the real driver arrive with promoteValues defaults (int64 that fits -> JS number, double 5.0 -> JS number 5), so the snapshot maps them to Int32/Double by value and a replayed int64 or integral double can be stored as a different numeric BSON type than it had
evidence: typed() maps JS numbers to Int32 (int32 range integer) or Double; the scopedCollection accessor offers no promoteValues:false. Never run against a real MongoDB (hard rule). Vectors stored as BSON arrays of doubles with integral values (0.0, 1.0) would come back as Int32.
fix_direction: read snapshot rows with promoteValues:false through a scoped accessor option, or check on the local work-DB copy that the corpus has no int64 / integral-double fields before relying on replay.

title: recovery repairs database rows only: the old session's local data/toc-migrated/<old> directory (removed by finish() on success) and the failed attempt's data/toc-migrated/<new> files are not reconciled after a kill, and a Windows pid reused by an unrelated process makes a dead holder's lock look live until the 6 h stale limit
evidence: recoverSnapshot touches only scopedCollection rows; acquireReingestLock uses process.kill(pid, 0).
fix_direction: record the lock holder's start time and compare; list local dirs in the manifest and reconcile them in recovery.

area: scripts/watch/lib/reingest-swap.mjs restoreOldRows (partial-row cleanup), run automatically by reingest-recover.mjs at startup
title: restore/recovery deletes every session whose sourceId is gdrive-<driveFileId> other than the old and the correct id, together with its turns/pages/claims/chunks. Such a sibling (an earlier fork of the same Drive file, the ISS-304/314 shape) legitimately existed before, is NOT in the snapshot, and is destroyed unrecoverably by any failed reingest or startup recovery.
evidence: checker scratch test on the BSON fake: seed old session + a sibling session 'dup-fork' (sourceId gdrive-<same file>) with a turn and a chunk; fail the ingest at step 8; after the 'restored and verified' result the sibling session, turn and chunk are all gone (false/false/false). Only preexistingSessionIds (the correct id) is protected.
fix_direction: at snapshot time record every session id already linked to the source (manifest.preexistingSessionIds = all of them, not only correctSessionId) and have restore delete only linked sessions created after the snapshot; or delete partial rows only for the ingest's own returned/derived new id.

title: the claim 'snapshot is read back and verified before the first delete' has no test: replacing the read-back call with a no-op leaves crash, snapshot and swap suites (64 tests) green.
evidence: checker mutation: 'readSnapshotFile(p.file);' in the try after atomicWrite replaced by 'void 0;' -> all three suites SURVIVED.
fix_direction: add a test where the hook/fs corrupts or truncates the file after rename (or atomicWrite is stubbed to write bad bytes) and assert replaceSessionRows throws with zero delete calls and no snapshot left.

area: scripts/watch/lib/reingest-swap.mjs ownedNewSessionIds (discovery of linked sessions outside the recorded pre-run set), restoreOldRows, recoverSnapshot
title: restore/recovery deletes ANY session linked to the Drive file that was not in the pre-run set, including one created by another writer after the manifest was written; the per-file reingest lock is taken only by reingest, not by run-watch --ingest (which uses data/.watch.lock)
repro: fake store; manifest written; before the run's restore (in-process ingest failure) or before startup recovery (kill at step 8) another process inserts session 'concurrent-ingest' {sourceId: gdrive-<file>} plus a turn; restore/recovery returns ok and the session and its turn are gone (A1, A2 in the checker's untracked test, both red). Reachable when the watcher's --ingest sees the file as new (no watch_state row / not in the month manifest), because reingest does not hold data/.watch.lock and --ingest does not take the reingest lock; the window is the whole ingest (transcription up to 2 h).
fix_direction: delete only ids the run itself can create: the planned correct id plus its deterministic fork id (correctSessionId + '-' + driveFileId.slice(0,6).toLowerCase(), see resolveSessionIdForIngest) and drop the linked-session discovery; and/or make run-watch --ingest honour the per-file reingest lock.

title: legacy-manifest handling: a cycle-0-shaped manifest (preexistingSessionIds present, no plannedNewSessionIds) still has discovery enabled and deletes a sibling; a manifest with neither field deletes the correct id even if it pre-existed. No such manifest exists in production (code unmerged), so low
repro: B1: cycle-0-shaped manifest + sibling dup-fork -> dup-fork gone; B2: manifest without both fields, correct id pre-existing with a turn -> session and turn gone
fix_direction: treat a manifest lacking plannedNewSessionIds as 'delete nothing by discovery'; refuse a no-field manifest whose correct id exists
